The Iglesia ni Cristo (INC) is holding a three-day rally for justice and peace from Sunday, November 16, until Tuesday, November 18, at the Quirino Grandstand in Manila.

The INC, a century-old Christian church of 2.8 million members, said it is calling for “a proper and transparent” investigation into the billion-peso controversy involving flood control projects. The church has been critical of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and supportive of Vice President Sara Duterte.

AFP’S OATH TO REMAIN NON-PARTISAN, DEFEND CONSTITUTION

LOOK: The Armed Forces of the Philippines says its personnel “renewed their sacred oath” to remain non-partisan and to defend the Constitution during an assembly at the AFP Grandstand in Quezon City on Sunday, Nov. 16.

The AFP says Bishop Noel Pantoja of the Philippine Council of Evangelical Churches was present in the assembly.

In one of the photos released by the AFP, Pantoja and other religious leaders were also seen praying over Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner Jr. and other officers.

The gathering came amid protests held in Metro Manila on Sunday, as well as rumors of destabilization plots.

One of the rally organizers was United People’s Initiative, a group led by retired military officials.
